Sadelle’s — SoHo, New York City

Sadelle’s is one of those places that always feels fun, and I loved that they served Alix Earle Margs but in a chic wine glass. A small detail, but it set the tone in the best way.

We ordered the tower, oysters, and veal dumplings, and I was genuinely happy with every single dish. The oysters came topped with sweet pickles, which added a flavor I didn’t know I needed, and they arrived on this dramatic chalice with ice underneath. Such a moment. The tower itself was generous, beautifully arranged, and everything on it was mind-blowing. The bagels were fresh, warm, and delivered on a stick like the Tobo bit from iCarly…very cute, very nostalgic. The grapefruit refresher was also bright, hydrating, and genuinely delicious.

The vibe inside is lively, buzzy, and feels like the kind of place where the morning easily slips into the afternoon. Perfect for a girls brunch or a weekend catch-up when you want great energy and dishes that truly deliver.

Fresh bagels, amazing smoked salmon, and that iconic brunch vibe. Always crowded but always worth it. A classic NYC treat every time.

Coffee was ok (maybe not too ok if you’re a snob), apple turnover was ok (apple sauce instead of sliced or chunked apples), prices slightly less than the west side but ok this is Harlem lol.

Will I come again? Prolly not cause I don’t really dare to venture too deep into Harlem alone. But is a naise place for reading and writing your friends long analogue letters cause there’s no pressure to hastily finish your drink and bugger off. No wifi but I do see wall sockets so undecided whether it’s a place to work. Coffee people here are naise too. Slightly young and rather alternative crowd.

I’ve been busy going from one place to another the past couple years, physically and also mentally as well, and haven’t taken as much time as I’d like to slow down and connect with people (actually in person, social media while a connector is not the same). 

Maybe that’s true for others also. We make plans and then inadvertently they get pushed off to some random date and then never materialize. So I was pleasantly surprised when I suggested a meet up with a new friend, she offered up a day and quickly found a great place (taking the mental load off of me to do so), and we made it happen! Just a coffee date filled pleasant and honest conversation. 

I’m working on savoring the small things which wind up being great things. Including more coffee and tea! ☕️😌🍵

Here’s the ugly truth: most owners only show up for the “big” rooms like national conferences, the flashy events, the places where it feels like opportunity should happen. But the real relationship equity? It gets built in the small rooms. The local ones. The ones you almost skip because you’re technically “on vacation.”

Tuesday night Chris and I made a last-minute call to hit the CTANJ (NJ Limo Association) holiday party. We were already in NYC for a Broadway show, and honestly, it would’ve been easy to say, “We’ll catch the next one.”

But showing up matters.
Not just at the national level… but in your own backyard.

It was good to see industry friends and clients — the kind of people who actually feel the ripple effects of your decisions, your work, your leadership. Local associations are where the pulse of the industry lives. And when you’re a business owner, presence is a strategy.

And yes — Chris and I absolutely turned a vacation into a work trip. Again.
At this point it’s basically a love language. 😅

Last night we headed to the PRLA Holiday Party (Pennsylvania Limo Association). Two states, two events, zero regrets — because this is how you stay connected, grounded, and relevant in the spaces that support your business year-round.

There’s also something mentally energizing about stepping into rooms where people get you. Entrepreneurial well-being is tied to connection, engagement, and feeling supported — not just grinding behind the scenes. When owners invest in their relationships (not just their operations), their stamina increases. 

If you’re an owner, here’s your nudge: Don’t underestimate the impact of just showing up, being present.

More from the road tomorrow — we’ll see what insights the next holiday party brings. 😉

Throwback from NYC a few weeks ago: went @a1recordshop . So glad it’s still there.

I wonder where Linda, Rich & Susan are now? Linda has such great handwriting - I’d like to know her full legacy.

I first went to A1 in about ‘07 when Ken Sekkle from Dub War proudly took us there. Where are you now sir?!

When we did, the door frame was covered in Polaroids from customers like DJ Premier & Phil Collins.

They weren’t there this time so I asked: turns out they have them stored, ready to be used for “30 years of A1” next year.

I’m always trying to look FWD>>, see what’s next. 

But some things of real musical & cultural value can’t easily be pulled into the future from the present’s thin air, they need to have been incubated & curated since the past.

Timeless Polaroid collections, small messy venues & incredible record stores are examples.

I love sharing Australian stuff and American stuff with y'all, so it's especially satisfying when I can share something from where those circles overlap in a Venn diagram.

The Chevrolet Caprice PPV was a car built, designed and engineered in Australia, but wearing a classic American nameplate and sold to American police departments.

It remains eternally frustrating how Holden developed the Zeta platform but so many of the vehicles planned to use it never came to be, while the Zeta-based Chevrolet Camaro wasn't offered in Australia.

It's also frustrating how after the VE Commodore-based Pontiac G8 was axed in 2009, GM decided to only sell the police fleet-only Caprice PPV. Bob Lutz had confirmed a Caprice for private buyers, only to walk this back.

The Caprice PPV was launched for model year 2011 and was offered as both a marked police cruiser and an unmarked detective's car – though any enthusiast criminal would have sniffed out that tail right away!

To an Aussie, seeing our Holden Statesman/Caprice as a police car is a bit surreal. This was the car for driving around prime ministers, not gangbangers! It's like seeing a Lincoln Town Car with a light bar on top. Why GM didn't sell this as a Buick Lucerne replacement is perplexing – it was sold in China as the Buick Park Avenue, after all.

The Caprice PPV was offered with either a 3.6 V6 or 6.0 V8, and initially used the dashboard of the base VE Commodore Omega.

Private buyers in the US could finally get a Holden again for model year 2014, based on the overhauled VF Commodore and badged as the Chevrolet SS.

Sadly, Australian GM production was in its final years, and would end in 2017. That meant the end of the Caprice PPV and SS.

GMC is coming to Australia, and I'm off to the launch of the Yukon Denali, locally remanufactured in right-hand drive.

The last time GM sold a full-size American SUV here was the Holden Suburban, a rebadged Chevrolet Suburban, from 1998 to 2000.

The Yukon will give GM a rival to the Toyota LandCruiser and Nissan Patrol, though with its pricing it's more of a rival for the Lexus LX. We won't get the longer Yukon XL.

What's all this got to do with this Envoy XL I saw in NYC? Well, I still find it fascinating that the extended-length version of GM's defunct "mid-size" (by American standards) body-on-frame SUV was actually longer than the regular length version of its full-size model!

The Envoy XL measured 207.6 inches (5273mm) long on a 129-inch (3277mm) wheelbase. A GMT800-series Yukon was 198.9 inches (5052mm) long on a 116-inch (2946mm) wheelbase, though it was 4.2 inches wider than the Envoy. 

That goes some way towards explaining why the long-wheelbase GMT370 SUVs (Envoy XL, Chevrolet Trailblazer EXT, Isuzu Ascender) were a bit awkward-looking.

It's also worth noting the GMT370 models' wheelbase was just an inch shorter than that of the Chevrolet Suburban and GMC Envoy XL.

Now, a brief overview of the GMT360, GMT370 and GMT305 family. The short- (GMT360) and long-wheelbase (GMT370) Trailblazer and Envoy models launched for model year 2002, along with the Oldsmobile Bravada which was SWB-only. This was Oldsmobile's last new model, and all three SUV lines had unique sheetmetal.

But then 2003 saw the launch of the Isuzu Ascender, a rebadged GMC Envoy. After Oldsmobile was shuttered in 2004, the Bravada's body was resurrected as the Buick Rainier. This bodywork was also used for the 2005 Saab 9-7X.

Engine choices included a 4.2 inline six and a 5.3 V8, with the Trailblazer and 9-7X also offering a 6.0 V8.

For over 26 years behind the DJ booth, I’ve never had an agent or booking agency. It’s always been about pure love for the music and getting my favorite people together under one roof. That energy has kept me smiling all these years.

To my chosen family who’s been by my side through every chapter, thank you for taking me as I am. I know I’m an ADHD mold breaker, and your loyalty has meant everything. For almost 30 years, it’s been pure debauchery and playing behind the best booths any DJ could ask for, surrounded by the most ridiculously good-looking crew on the planet.

What DJs don’t talk about is the family cycle. In the early days, all your friends show up. But over time, people settle down, get married, have kids, and slowly disappear from the dancefloor. My ADHD never let me stop, so I kept finding new people to dance with. From the original rave crew “The Untouchables, to the Dirty Dozen, and then Kuya and Filipino Mafia to the restaurant heads, brothers Mort & Fels, my brother Chachi, brother Joe Johnson, my bestie brother Greg. I have been truly blessed by what ever you pray to for blessing me with being able to DJ for 7 cycles of family. 26 + years of truly feeling alive.

Santa’s Winter Wonderland at Watermark, one of New York City’s most magical holiday attractions, is returning for its 6th year to the Seaport District at Watermark, the 10,000-square-foot outdoor bar and restaurant located on Pier 15. This is an over-the-top winter wonderland with faux snow,  holiday cocktails and spiked hot chocolate as well as treats like toasted s’mores. 

This is your escape to the North Pole and fun for all ages with the candy-cane-filled hallway and Santa’s Game Room. Hop in santas sleigh set against the Brooklyn skyline for great photo ops, or the heated glass houses to enjoy in warmth.

Visited @watermarkny Santa’s Winter Wonderland at Pier 15 for the first time this year🎄. It had a cozy, festive vibe — but I’ll be honest, it didn’t quite live up to what I imagined. Not trying to be a grinch. It was also much smaller than expected… but hey, to each their own. 

And listen — I do get serious NYC holiday FOMO sometimes, so I’m actually glad I finally tried it and saw it for myself ✔️.

On the plus side: we did get hot chocolate and cake pops with our package. My hubby really enjoyed his hot chocolate 🍫 — until he realized all the marshmallows were hiding at the bottom of the cup 😂.

Still, it’s a cute spot for families with little ones 🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒— just not a must-return for me. Sometimes you’ve gotta try a place once to know where it lands.
